items.name: Cmd
items.signature:
{
	args : List(OsStr),
	clear_envs : Bool,
	envs : List((OsStr, OsStr)),
	program : OsStr,
	cwd_value : List(Path),
	stdin_value : [Default, Inherit, Null, Bytes(List(U8)), Pipe],
	stdout_value : [Default, Inherit, Null, Capture, Pipe, Tee],
	stderr_value : [Default, Inherit, Null, Capture, Pipe, Tee],
	timeout_value : U64,
	output_limit_value : U64,
	pending_limit_value : U64,
	manage_tree_value : Bool,
	merge_stderr_value : Bool,
}
items.docs:
Build and run child processes with native-safe programs, arguments, and
environment values.

Use `run!` when exit status and output are data your application handles:

```roc
output = Cmd.new("roc")
	.arg("version")
	.timeout_ms(5_000)
	.run!()?

match output.status {
	Exited(0) => Stdout.write_bytes!(output.stdout_bytes)
	Exited(code) => Err(CommandFailed(code))
	Signaled(signal) => Err(CommandSignaled(signal))
}
```
items.head: Cmd

items.name: exec!
items.signature: OsStr, List(OsStr) => Try({}, [ExecFailed({ command : Str, exit_code : I32 }), FailedToGetExitCode({ command : Str, err : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Simplest way to execute a command by name with arguments.
Stdin, stdout, and stderr are inherited from the parent process.

If you want to capture the output, use [exec_output!] instead.

```roc
Cmd.exec!("echo", ["hello world"])?
```

items.name: exec_cmd!
items.signature: Cmd => Try({}, [ExecCmdFailed({ command : Str, exit_code : I32 }), FailedToGetExitCode({ command : Str, err : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Execute a Cmd (using the builder pattern).
Stdin, stdout, and stderr are inherited from the parent process.

You should prefer using [exec!] instead, only use this if you want to use [env], [envs] or [clear_envs].
If you want to capture the output, use [exec_output!] instead.

```roc
Cmd.new("cargo")
    .arg("build")
    .env("RUST_BACKTRACE", "1")
    .exec_cmd!()?
```

items.name: exec_output!
items.signature: Cmd => Try({ stdout_utf8 : Str, stderr_utf8_lossy : Str }, [StdoutContainsInvalidUtf8({ cmd_str : Str, err : [BadUtf8({ problem : _, index : U64 })] }), NonZeroExitCode({ command : Str, exit_code : I32, stdout_utf8_lossy : Str, stderr_utf8_lossy : Str }), FailedToGetExitCode({ command : Str, err : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Execute command and capture stdout and stderr as UTF-8 strings.
Invalid UTF-8 sequences are replaced with the Unicode replacement character.

Use [exec_output_bytes!] instead if you want to capture the output in the original form as bytes.
[exec_output_bytes!] may also be used for maximum performance, because you may be able to avoid unnecessary UTF-8 conversions.

```roc
cmd_output =
    Cmd.new("echo")
        .args(["Hi"])
        .exec_output!()?

Stdout.line!("Echo output: ${cmd_output.stdout_utf8}")?
```

items.name: exec_output_bytes!
items.signature: Cmd => Try({ stderr_bytes : List(U8), stdout_bytes : List(U8) }, [NonZeroExitCodeB({ exit_code : I32, stdout_bytes : List(U8), stderr_bytes : List(U8) }), FailedToGetExitCodeB(IOErr)])
items.docs:
Execute command and capture stdout and stderr in the original form as bytes.

Use [exec_output!] instead if you want to get the output as UTF-8 strings.

```roc
cmd_output =
    Cmd.new("echo")
        .args(["Hi"])
        .exec_output_bytes!()?

Stdout.line!("${Str.inspect(cmd_output)}")? # {stderr_bytes: [], stdout_bytes: [72, 105, 10]}
```

items.name: exec_exit_code!
items.signature: Cmd => Try(I32, [FailedToGetExitCode({ command : Str, err : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Execute a command and return its exit code.
Stdin, stdout, and stderr are inherited from the parent process.

You should prefer using [exec!] or [exec_cmd!] instead, only use this if you want to take a specific action based on a **specific non-zero exit code**.
For example, `roc check` returns exit code 1 if there are errors, and exit code 2 if there are only warnings.
So, you could use `exec_exit_code!` to ignore warnings on `roc check`.

```roc
exit_code = Cmd.new("cat").arg("non_existent.txt").exec_exit_code!()?
```

items.name: new
items.docs:
Create a new command with the given program name. Use a function that starts with `exec_` to execute it.

```roc
cmd = Cmd.new("ls")
```

items.name: new_str
items.docs:
Create a new command from a dynamic `Str`. String literals can be passed
directly to [new].

items.name: cwd
items.docs:
Set the child working directory without changing the parent directory.
Use an absolute executable path or a bare PATH name: resolving a relative
executable against cwd is platform-specific.

items.name: stdin
items.signature: Cmd, [Default, Inherit, Null, Bytes(List(U8)), Pipe] -> Cmd
items.docs:
Bytes supplies and closes stdin automatically. Pipe supports Child.write!.
Default is Null for run!/exec_output!, Inherit for spawn!/exec_cmd!.

items.name: stdout
items.signature: Cmd, [Default, Inherit, Null, Capture, Pipe, Tee] -> Cmd
items.docs:
Capture retains bytes; Pipe queues tagged Child.read! events; Tee captures
and forwards to the parent. Default captures for run!/exec_output!, and
inherits for spawn!/exec_cmd!. Tee exposes a pipe, not a terminal, to the child.

items.name: stderr
items.signature: Cmd, [Default, Inherit, Null, Capture, Pipe, Tee] -> Cmd
items.docs: Configure stderr independently, with the same modes and defaults as stdout.

items.name: timeout_ms
items.docs: Zero disables the execution deadline. It covers output draining too.

items.name: output_limit
items.docs:
Combined capture budget in bytes (default 16 MiB). Exceeding it cancels
the command and returns OutputLimit with the retained partial output.

items.name: pending_limit
items.docs:
Combined unread Pipe event budget (default 1 MiB). Consume events with
Child.read! while running; exceeding this budget cancels the child.

items.name: manage_tree
items.docs:
Also terminate descendants on cancellation, using a Unix process group
or Windows Job Object. Disabled by default; descendants must not escape it.

items.name: merge_stderr
items.docs:
Send both child streams into one OS pipe using stdout's mode and budget.
This preserves kernel write order; separate streams have no total ordering.

items.name: run!
items.docs:
Nonzero exits and signal termination are returned as status data.
Defaults to null stdin and captured stdout/stderr. Successful completion
waits for output EOF; deadlines include draining and tee forwarding.

items.name: spawn!
items.docs: Start a managed child immediately. Default streams are inherited.

items.name: arg
items.docs:
Add a single argument to the command.
❗ Shell features like variable substitution (e.g. `$FOO`), glob patterns (e.g. `*.txt`), ... are not available.

```roc
cmd = Cmd.new("ls").arg("-l")
```

items.name: args
items.docs:
Add multiple arguments to the command.
❗ Shell features like variable substitution (e.g. `$FOO`), glob patterns (e.g. `*.txt`), ... are not available.

```roc
cmd = Cmd.new("ls").args(["-l", "-a"])
```

Add multiple dynamic `Str` arguments. Lists of string literals can be passed
directly to [args].

items.name: env
items.docs:
Add a single environment variable to the command.


```roc
cmd = Cmd.new("env").env("FOO", "bar") # add the environment variable "FOO" with value "bar"
```

items.name: env_str
items.docs:
Add a dynamic `Str` environment variable. String literals can be passed
directly to [env].

items.name: envs
items.docs:
Add multiple environment variables to the command.

```roc
cmd = Cmd.new("env").envs([("FOO", "bar"), ("BAZ", "qux")])
```

items.name: envs_str
items.docs:
Add multiple dynamic `Str` environment variables. Lists of literal pairs can
be passed directly to [envs].

items.name: clear_envs
items.docs:
Clear all environment variables before running the command.
Only environment variables added via `env` or `envs` will be available.
Useful if you want a clean command run that does not behave unexpectedly if the user has some env var set.

```roc
cmd =
    Cmd.new("env")
        .clear_envs()
        .env("ONLY_THIS", "visible")
```

items.name: check_available!
items.docs:
Report whether `command` can be found on the system as something runnable.

A bare name (like `"git"`) is looked up across the `PATH` entries; a name
containing a path separator is checked as-is. On Windows the candidate
extensions come from `%PATHEXT%`.

On Unix this checks for an executable bit; a directory is not reported even
though it carries one, though a symbolic link to a directory is a rare
exception.

items.docs:
Return all environment variables as native name/value pairs.

Native non-Unicode values are preserved. Iteration order is unspecified
and may differ between calls or operating systems.

items.name: var!
items.docs:
Reads the given environment variable.

Returns `Err(VarNotFound(name))` if the variable is not set.

items.name: var_str!
items.docs: Reads the given environment variable as a string if its native value is valid text.

items.name: cwd!
items.docs:
Reads the [current working directory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_directory)
from the environment.

Returns `Err(CwdUnavailable)` if the cwd cannot be determined.

items.name: set_cwd!
items.docs:
Change the process current working directory.

Returns `Err(InvalidCwd(err))` when the path cannot be used as a working
directory. The process-wide change remains in effect until changed again.

items.name: exe_path!
items.docs:
Gets the path to the currently-running executable.

Returns `Err(ExePathUnavailable)` if the path cannot be determined.

items.name: program_name!
items.docs:
Gets the program name supplied by the process launcher as its first argument.

This is conventionally the executable name or path, but launchers may supply
another value. Unlike [`exe_path!`](#exe_path!), it is returned as an
[`OsStr`](OsStr), preserving the value exactly without treating it as a path.
Returns `Err(ProgramNameUnavailable)` if the launcher supplied no first argument.

items.name: create_temp_dir!
items.docs:
Atomically create a private directory in the system temporary directory.
The caller owns cleanup. Unix directories have mode 0700.

items.name: create_temp_dir_with_prefix!
items.docs: Create a private temporary directory with a filename prefix.

items.name: create_temp_dir_in!
items.docs:
Create a private temporary directory under an existing parent directory.
Prefixes cannot contain separators, colons, NUL, or be `.` or `..`.

items.name: with_temp_dir!
items.signature: (Path.Path => Try(a, err)) => Try(a, [TempDirErr(IOErr), CallbackErr(err), CleanupErr(IOErr, Path.Path), CallbackAndCleanupErr(err, IOErr, Path.Path)])
items.docs:
Run a callback with a private directory and delete the directory afterward.
Cleanup is attempted after callback success and failure. If both fail, both errors are returned.

```roc
Env.with_temp_dir!(|directory| {
	file = Path.join(directory, "result.txt")
	Path.write_utf8!(file, "temporary data")?
	Path.read_utf8!(file)
})?
```

items.docs: Gets the default directory for temporary files.

items.docs: A byte offset from the start, current logical position, or end of a file.
items.head: SeekFrom

items.name: Reader
items.docs:
Represents a buffered file reader.

The file is automatically closed when the last reference to the reader is
dropped. It wraps an opaque host-side `BufReader<File>` handle.
Aliases share one cursor, including bytes buffered by line or binary reads.
items.head: Reader

items.name: to_inspect
items.docs: Render the reader without exposing its host handle.

items.name: read_line!
items.docs:
Read bytes up to and including the next newline from this buffered reader.

Returns an empty list at EOF.

items.name: read_up_to!
items.docs:
Read at most `max_bytes` bytes. Short reads are valid, even before EOF.
For a positive maximum, an empty list means EOF. Zero performs no I/O.
Returned bytes remain valid after later reads or seeks.

items.name: read_exactly!
items.docs:
Read exactly `count` bytes, or report `FileUnexpectedEOF`.
Zero succeeds without I/O. Errors may consume bytes; partial data is
not returned and the cursor is not restored.

items.name: position!
items.docs: Return the byte position of the next read, accounting for buffered bytes.

items.name: seek!
items.docs:
Move the shared cursor and return its new absolute byte position.
Seeking past EOF does not extend the file. Invalid offsets and sources
that cannot seek report FileErr. A failed seek need not restore the cursor.
Aliases of this reader observe the same cursor.

items.name: chunks
items.docs:
Lazily read nonempty chunks of at most `max_bytes` from this reader.
Zero is rejected immediately with InvalidChunkSize. Construction does
no I/O; each pull reads from the current shared cursor. Chunk boundaries
do not correspond to records, newlines, or text encoding boundaries.
EOF ends the stream; a read error yields one Err item, then ends.
Follow the returned continuation when pulling. To resume after EOF
and a seek, create a new stream. Retained chunks remain valid.
The stream keeps the file open while it retains a reader. Its terminal
continuation holds no reader. Process chunks individually to bound memory;
Stream.collect! accumulates every chunk and does not propagate Err items.

items.name: open_reader!
items.docs:
Open a file for buffered reading using the default buffer capacity.

Failing to open reports the path, using the same `PathErr` as the
whole-file operations so both combine in one error type.

```roc
reader = File.open_reader!("LICENSE")?
line = reader.read_line!()?
```

items.docs: Open a file for buffered reading using a specific buffer capacity.

items.name: send!
items.docs:
Validate and send an HTTP request.

The request URI must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL accepted by Url.
Invalid URLs return InvalidUrl before any host effect occurs. Fragments
are removed because they are client-side identifiers and are not sent.

```roc
request = Request.from_method(GET).with_uri("https://www.roc-lang.org")
response = Http.send!(request)?
```

items.name: with_json_body
items.docs:
Encode a value as JSON and set it as the request body.

This uses Roc's builtin JSON encoder, so the value's type determines the
encoder through static dispatch.

items.name: send_json!
items.docs: Encode a value as JSON, attach it to the request body, and send it.

items.name: get_utf8!
items.docs:
Perform an HTTP GET and decode the response body as a UTF-8 `Str`.

The argument is a validated Url. Quoted literals work through
Url.from_quote; dynamic strings should be passed through Url.parse.

```roc
hello_str = Http.get_utf8!("http://localhost:8000")?
```

items.name: decode_json_response
items.docs:
Decode a response body as JSON.

This uses Roc's builtin JSON parser, so the expected result type
determines the parser through static dispatch.

items.name: get!
items.docs:
Perform an HTTP GET and decode the response body as JSON.

The argument is a validated Url. JSON parser failures are returned as
JsonErr(_).

```roc
payload : Try({ foo : Str }, _)
payload = Http.get!("http://localhost:8000")
```

items.name: IOErr
items.signature:
[
	AlreadyExists,
	BrokenPipe,
	Interrupted,
	IsADirectory,
	NotFound,
	NotADirectory,
	Other(Str),
	OutOfMemory,
	PermissionDenied,
	Unsupported,
]
items.docs:
Represents an I/O error that can occur during platform operations.

**NotFound** - An entity was not found, often a file.

**PermissionDenied** - The operation lacked the necessary privileges to complete.

**BrokenPipe** - The operation failed because a pipe was closed.

**AlreadyExists** - An entity already exists, often a file.

**Interrupted** - This operation was interrupted. Interrupted operations can typically be retried.

**IsADirectory** - A filesystem operation expected a non-directory path.

**NotADirectory** - A filesystem operation expected a directory path.

**Unsupported** - This operation is unsupported on this platform. This means that the operation can never succeed.

**OutOfMemory** - An operation could not be completed, because it failed to allocate enough memory.

**Other** - A custom error that does not fall under any other I/O error kind.
items.head: IOErr

items.name: get!
items.docs:
Returns the most preferred locale for the system or application.

POSIX locale names are normalized by removing encoding and modifier
suffixes and replacing underscores with hyphens. The special `C` and
`POSIX` locales are not language tags and are ignored.

Returns `Err(NotAvailable)` if the locale cannot be determined.

Values are normalized and validated as described by `get!`. Invalid values
are omitted, and duplicates are removed case-insensitively while preserving
preference order.

items.docs:
TODO: Restore generic parser_for and encoder_for helpers when the compiler
no longer treats auto-derived `_` declarations in platforms as hosted:
https://github.com/roc-lang/roc/issues/10162
Convert an OS string to a string if its raw representation is valid text.

items.name: to_bytes
items.docs:
Convert an OS string to the bytes that represent it, for writing to a byte
stream such as [Stdout.write_bytes!] or [Stderr.write_bytes!].

UTF-8 text and Unix OS strings return their exact bytes, so non-Unicode Unix
data is preserved. Windows OS strings are UTF-16 code units rather than bytes,
so they are encoded as UTF-8 with unpaired surrogates replaced by U+FFFD;
that conversion is lossy and must not be used for roundtripping.

items.name: display
items.docs:

with U+FFFD. This representation is lossy and must not be used for roundtripping.

items.name: Path
items.docs:
Construct and operate on byte-preserving paths. Native Unix
bytes and Windows UTF-16 units are preserved across host effects; use
`display` only when a lossy human-readable representation is appropriate.

Quoted literals create UTF-8 paths, and `join` appends one path component:

```roc
Path.create_all!("config")?
config_file = Path.join("config", "app.json")
Path.write_utf8!(config_file, "{}")?
```
items.head: Path

items.name: is_file!
items.docs:
Returns `Bool.True` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

This function does not traverse symbolic links; symbolic links (including
broken ones) return `Bool.False`.
Sockets, FIFOs, devices, and other special filesystem objects also return `Bool.False`.

items.name: is_dir!
items.docs:
Returns `Bool.True` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a directory.

This function does not traverse symbolic links; symbolic links (including
broken ones) return `Bool.False`.
Sockets, FIFOs, devices, and other special filesystem objects also return `Bool.False`.

items.name: is_sym_link!
items.docs:
Returns `Bool.True` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a symbolic link.

This function will not traverse symbolic links - it checks whether the path
itself is a symlink.
Sockets, FIFOs, devices, and other special filesystem objects return `Bool.False`.

items.name: exists!
items.docs: Returns `True` if the path exists on disk.

items.name: type!
items.signature: Path => Try([IsFile, IsDir, IsSymLink, IsOther], [PathErr(IOErr, Path)])
items.docs:
Return the type of the path if the path exists on disk.

`IsOther` represents sockets, FIFOs, block and character devices, and any
platform-specific object that is not a regular file, directory, or symbolic
link. On Windows this includes unrecognized reparse-point types.

items.name: absolute!
items.docs: Make a path absolute without requiring it to exist. This does not resolve symlinks.

items.name: canonicalize!
items.docs: Resolve an existing path, including symbolic links, to its absolute native path.

items.name: copy!
items.signature: Path, Path => Try({}, [CopyErr({ operation : Str, source : Path, destination : Path, error : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Copy a regular file and its permissions, replacing the destination file.
Rejects same-file copies (including hard-link aliases) and special files.

items.name: copy_dir!
items.signature: Path, Path => Try({}, [CopyErr({ operation : Str, source : Path, destination : Path, error : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Copy a directory tree into a new destination, following symbolic links.
Missing destination parent directories are created.
Permissions are preserved; timestamps, ownership, ACLs and other metadata are not.
Errors may leave a partial destination. Cycles and overlapping source/destination trees are rejected.

items.name: copy_dir_with!
items.signature: Path, Path, { symlinks : [Follow, Preserve], destination : [RequireNew, Merge] } => Try({}, [CopyErr({ operation : Str, source : Path, destination : Path, error : IOErr })])
items.docs:
Choose whether to preserve links and whether to merge an existing destination tree.
Merge replaces regular files. Existing destination directory symlinks are rejected.

items.name: replace_utf8!
items.docs:
Replace every occurrence of `pattern` with `replacement` in the UTF-8 file
at this path.

This reads the whole file, substitutes, and writes it back, so it is not
atomic: a failure mid-write can leave the file partially written, exactly
as a bare [write_utf8!] would.

Errors report `from`; a failure may still concern `to`, such as its
parent directory not existing.

items.name: millis!
items.docs: Sleep for the specified number of milliseconds.

items.name: seconds!
items.docs:
Sleep for the specified number of seconds.

The duration is truncated to whole milliseconds, so `Sleep.seconds!(1.5)`
sleeps for 1500 ms. Negative and `NaN` durations return immediately, and
durations past [U64.highest] milliseconds saturate there.

items.name: line!
items.docs:
Write the given string to [standard error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_error_(stderr)),
followed by a newline.

> To write to `stderr` without the newline, see [Stderr.write!].

items.name: write!
items.docs:
Write the given string to [standard error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_error_(stderr)).

Most terminals will not actually display strings that are written to them until they receive a newline,
so this may appear to do nothing until you write a newline!

> To write to `stderr` with a newline at the end, see [Stderr.line!].

items.name: write_bytes!
items.docs:
Write the given bytes to [standard error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_error_(stderr)).

Most terminals will not actually display content that are written to them until they receive a newline,
so this may appear to do nothing until you write a newline!

items.name: line!
items.docs:
Read a line from [standard input](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_input_(stdin)).

> This task will block the program from continuing until `stdin` receives a newline character
(e.g. because the user pressed Enter in the terminal), so using it can result in the appearance of the
program having gotten stuck. It's often helpful to print a prompt first, so
the user knows it's necessary to enter something before the program will continue.

items.name: bytes!
items.docs:
Read bytes from [standard input](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_input_(stdin)).
This function can read no more than 16,384 bytes at a time. Use [read_to_end!] if you need more.

> This is typically used in combination with [Tty.enable_raw_mode!],
which disables default terminal behaviour and allows reading input
without buffering until Enter key is pressed.

items.name: read_to_end!
items.docs:
Read all bytes from [standard input](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_input_(stdin))
until [EOF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End-of-file) in this source.

items.name: line!
items.docs:
Write the given string to [standard output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_output_(stdout)),
followed by a newline.

> To write to `stdout` without the newline, see [Stdout.write!].

items.name: write!
items.docs:
Write the given string to [standard output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_output_(stdout)).

Note that many terminals will not actually display strings that are written to them until they receive a newline,
so this may appear to do nothing until you write a newline!

> To write to `stdout` with a newline at the end, see [Stdout.line!].

items.name: write_bytes!

Write the given bytes to [standard output](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_streams#Standard_output_(stdout)).

Note that many terminals will not actually display content that is written to them until they receive a newline,

items.docs: Close the listener. Repeated closes succeed.

items.docs:
Bind an address and listen. Port zero reserves an OS-assigned port until
this listener is closed. The timeout includes hostname resolution.

items.name: Stream
items.docs:
Represents a TCP stream.

The connection is automatically closed when the last reference to the
stream is dropped. It wraps an opaque host-side `BufReader<TcpStream>`
handle.
items.head: Stream

items.name: to_inspect
items.docs: Render the stream without exposing its host handle.

items.name: read_up_to!
items.docs: Read up to a number of bytes, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds.

items.name: read_exactly!
items.docs:
Read an exact number of bytes, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds.

`TcpUnexpectedEOF` is returned if the stream ends before the specified
number of bytes is reached.

items.name: read_until!
items.docs:
Read until a delimiter or EOF is reached, consuming at most `max_bytes`
and waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds.
If found, the delimiter is included as the last byte. Returns
`TcpReadLimitExceeded(max_bytes)` if the delimiter was not found within
the limit.

items.name: read_line!
items.docs:
Read at most `max_bytes` through a newline (`\n`, byte 10) or EOF as
UTF-8, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds. If found, the newline
is included as the last character.

items.name: write!
items.docs: Write bytes, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds.

items.name: write_utf8!
items.docs: Write a string as UTF-8, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds.

items.name: connect!
items.docs:
Opens a TCP connection, waiting at most `timeout_ms` milliseconds across
DNS resolution and all resolved addresses. A zero timeout fails immediately.

```roc
# Connect to localhost:8080
stream = Tcp.connect!("localhost", 8080, 5_000)?
```

Valid hostnames look like `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`, or `roc-lang.org`.

items.name: connect_err_to_str
items.docs: Convert a `ConnectErr` to a `Str` you can print.

items.name: stream_err_to_str
items.docs: Convert a `StreamErr` to a `Str` you can print.

items.name: enable_raw_mode!
items.docs:
Enable terminal [raw mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_mode) to disable some default terminal behaviour.

This leads to the following changes:
- Input will not be echoed to the terminal screen.
- Input will be sent straight to the program instead of being buffered (= collected) until the Enter key is pressed.
- Special keys like Backspace and CTRL+C will not be processed by the terminal driver but will be passed to the program.

items.name: disable_raw_mode!
items.docs: Revert terminal to default behaviour

items.name: Url
items.signature:
{
	scheme : [Http, Https],
	host : Str,
	port : [None, Some(U16)],
	path : Str,
	query : [None, Some(Str)],
	fragment : [None, Some(Str)],
}
items.docs:
A validated HTTP or HTTPS URL implemented entirely in Roc.

This is deliberately stricter than a browser parser. Hosts must be ASCII
DNS names, dotted-decimal IPv4 addresses, or bracketed IPv6 addresses made
from hexadecimal groups with optional :: elision. IPv4-in-IPv6 and Unicode
domain names are intentionally unsupported.
items.head: Url

items.name: ParseErr
items.signature:
[
		CredentialsNotAllowed,
		EmptyHost,
		InternationalHostUnsupported,
		InvalidCharacter(U8),
		InvalidHost(Str),
		InvalidIpv4(Str),
		InvalidIpv6(Str),
		InvalidPercentEncoding(U64),
		InvalidPort(Str),
		MissingAuthority,
		MissingScheme,
		PortOutOfRange(U64),
		UnsupportedScheme(Str),
	]
items.docs:
A reason a URL or relative reference could not be parsed.

This error set describes this module's strict HTTP/HTTPS subset. Inputs
that browsers might repair, such as missing authority slashes or
backslashes, are rejected instead.
items.head: ParseErr

items.name: parse
items.docs:
Parse a dynamic string as an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL.

The input must contain an explicit scheme and authority. Its host is
lowercased, default ports are removed, dot path segments are normalized,
and non-ASCII path, query, and fragment bytes are percent-encoded.

items.name: from_quote
items.docs:
Convert a quoted literal to a URL using the same validation as parse.

Roc calls this automatically when a quoted literal is expected to have
type Url. A rejected literal reports a descriptive BadQuotedBytes error.

items.name: parser_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (state -> Try({ value : Url, rest : state }, err))
		where [
			encoding.parse_str : encoding, state -> Try({ value : Str, rest : state }, err),
			encoding.invalid_value : encoding, state -> err,
		]
items.docs: Parse a URL from a string value supplied by a generic encoding.

items.name: encoder_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (Url, state -> Try(state, err))
		where [
			encoding.encode_str : Str, state -> Try(state, err),
		]
items.docs: Encode a URL as its canonical string through a generic encoding.

items.name: to_str
items.docs:
Serialize the URL in a stable normalized ASCII form.

Scheme and DNS host names are lowercase, default ports are omitted,
paths are absolute, and IPv6 addresses use eight unpadded groups.

items.name: to_inspect
items.docs: Render a URL for debugging and test failures.

items.name: is_eq
items.docs: Compare URLs by their canonical serialized representation.

items.name: to_hash
items.docs: Hash URLs consistently with canonical equality.

items.name: scheme
items.docs: Return Http or Https.

items.name: host
items.docs:
Return the canonical host.

IPv6 brackets are omitted; to_str includes them where required.

items.name: port
items.docs:
Return an explicit non-default port.

Ports 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS are canonicalized to None.

items.name: path
items.docs: Return the absolute percent-encoded path, always beginning with slash.

items.name: query
items.docs:
Return the percent-encoded query without its leading question mark.

None and Some("") distinguish no query from a present empty query.

items.name: fragment
items.docs:
Return the percent-encoded fragment without its leading hash.

None and Some("") distinguish no fragment from a present empty fragment.

items.name: without_fragment
items.docs: Return this URL without its fragment. HTTP never transmits fragments.

items.name: resolve
items.docs:
Resolve a strict relative reference or absolute web URL against this URL.

Root-relative, path-relative, query-only, and fragment-only references
are supported. Scheme-relative references are rejected.

items.name: append_path_segments
items.docs:
Append unencoded path segments.

Each list item is one segment, so slash characters inside an item are
percent-encoded rather than treated as separators.

items.name: append_query_param
items.docs:
Append one application/x-www-form-urlencoded query pair.

Existing parameters, ordering, duplicate names, and the fragment are
preserved.

items.name: query_pairs
items.docs:
Decode the query into ordered name/value pairs.

Plus signs decode as spaces, percent escapes decode as UTF-8 bytes,
parameters without equals receive an empty value, and duplicates remain.

items.name: with_query
items.docs:
Replace or remove the query.

Some("") produces a present empty query. The supplied query may contain
Unicode but must otherwise already obey URL query syntax.

items.name: with_fragment
items.docs:
Replace or remove the fragment.

Some("") produces a present empty fragment. Unicode is percent-encoded.
